subject: math
title: Area of Parallelograms and Triangles
seo_title: Grade 5 Area of Parallelograms and Triangles Math Worksheets (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Use the area relationships among rectangles, parallelograms, and triangles to develop the formulas for the area of a parallelogram and the area of a triangle, and solve related problems
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on area for the Ontario curriculum: rectangles, parallelograms (base × height), triangles (base × height ÷ 2), shapes with the same area but different perimeters, and word problems about gardens, flags and rinks. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Parallelogram: base × height. Triangle: base × height ÷ 2.
key_sub: The height meets the base at a right angle, so a slanted side is not the height. A triangle is half of a parallelogram with the same base and height. Shapes with the same area can have different perimeters.
body_html:
The big idea: start from the rectangle

The area of a rectangle is base × height. Area is the space inside a shape. It is measured in square units, like cm² and m². Parallelograms and triangles can be turned into rectangles, so you can find their area too. The height is always measured at a right angle to the base. It is drawn as a dashed line with a small square at the corner.

Parallelograms: A = base × height

Cut the triangle off one end and slide it to the other end. The parallelogram becomes a rectangle with the same base and the same height. So the area does not change.

Triangles: A = base × height ÷ 2

Two copies of a triangle fit together to make a parallelogram with the same base and height. So a triangle is half of it. In a right triangle, the two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height.

Example

A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a height of 7 cm. Find the area.

Multiply the base by the height: 10 × 7 = 70. Take half: 70 ÷ 2 = 35.

Answer: 35 cm²

Same area, different perimeters

Area is the space inside. Perimeter is the distance around. Two shapes can have the same area but different perimeters. A long, thin rectangle has a greater perimeter than one that is close to a square.

Example

A rectangle is 3 m by 8 m. Find a rectangle with the same area but a smaller perimeter.

Area: 3 × 8 = 24 m². 4 × 6 = 24 too. Perimeters: 3 + 8 + 3 + 8 = 22 m and 4 + 6 + 4 + 6 = 20 m.

Answer: 4 m by 6 m

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the slanted side as the heightUse the dashed height at a right angle to the base
Triangle: 14 × 12 = 168Take half: 14 × 12 ÷ 2 = 84
Parallelogram: 12 × 8 ÷ 2 = 48No half for a parallelogram: 12 × 8 = 96
Thinking the same area means the same perimeterAdd the sides of each shape to check
Writing 84 m for an areaArea is in square units: 84 m²

faq.q: What do Grade 5 students learn about area in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: In Grade 5 (Spatial Sense), students use rectangles to develop the formulas for the area of a parallelogram (base × height) and a triangle (base × height ÷ 2) and solve problems with them (E2.5). They also show that shapes with the same area can have different perimeters (E2.6).

faq.q: Why do you divide by 2 to find the area of a triangle?
faq.a: Two copies of the same triangle fit together to make a parallelogram with the same base and height. The triangle is half of it, so its area is base × height ÷ 2.

faq.q: Is the slanted side of a parallelogram its height?
faq.a: No. The height is the distance straight up from the base, at a right angle to it. The slanted side is always longer than the height, so using it gives an area that is too big.

faq.q: Can two shapes have the same area but different perimeters?
faq.a: Yes. A 2 cm by 9 cm rectangle and a 3 cm by 6 cm rectangle both have an area of 18 cm², but their perimeters are 22 cm and 18 cm.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: A = base × height = 15 × 7 = 105 m².

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 72 m². It is 9 m long. How wide is it?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 9 × ? = 72. 72 ÷ 9 = 8 m. Check: 9 × 8 = 72.

items.q: A rectangle is 25 cm long and 8 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: A = length × width = 25 × 8 = 200 cm².

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 84 cm². It is 12 cm long. How wide is it?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 12 × ? = 84. 84 ÷ 12 = 7 cm. Check: 12 × 7 = 84.

items.q: A rectangle is 14 m long and 12 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: A = length × width = 14 × 12 = 168 m².

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: A = base × height = 13 × 9 = 117 m².

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: A = base × height = 11 × 4 = 44 cm².

items.q: A square has sides of 7 m. What is its area?
items.e: All four sides are 7 m, so A = 7 × 7 = 49 m². (4 × 7 = 28 is the perimeter.)

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: A = base × height = 11 × 5 = 55 cm². Adding the sides (11 + 5 + 11 + 5 = 32) gives the perimeter, not the area.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 56 cm². It is 8 cm long. How wide is it?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 8 × ? = 56. 56 ÷ 8 = 7 cm. Check: 8 × 7 = 56.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: A = base × height = 12 × 6 = 72 cm². Adding the sides (12 + 6 + 12 + 6 = 36) gives the perimeter, not the area.

items.q: A rectangle is 8 m by 5 m. Which number sentence gives its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 8 × 5 = 40 m². 2 × (8 + 5) = 26 is the perimeter.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: A = base × height = 7 × 4 = 28 cm².

items.q: A square has sides of 9 cm. What is its area?
items.e: All four sides are 9 cm, so A = 9 × 9 = 81 cm². (4 × 9 = 36 is the perimeter.)

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm². What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Count the squares: 2 rows of 7 is 2 × 7 = 14 squares. Each square is 1 cm², so the area is 14 cm². (18 cm is the perimeter: the distance around.)

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm². What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Count the squares: 3 rows of 5 is 3 × 5 = 15 squares. Each square is 1 cm², so the area is 15 cm². (16 cm is the perimeter: the distance around.)

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: A = base × height = 14 × 8 = 112 m². Adding the sides (14 + 8 + 14 + 8 = 44) gives the perimeter, not the area.

items.q: A rectangle is 32 m long and 15 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: A = length × width = 32 × 15 = 480 m².

items.q: Which unit is best for the area of a classroom floor?
items.e: Area is measured in square units. A classroom floor is a few metres long, so square metres (m²) fit best.

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm². What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Count the squares: 3 rows of 8 is 3 × 8 = 24 squares. Each square is 1 cm², so the area is 24 cm². (22 cm is the perimeter: the distance around.)

items.q: A rectangle is 9 cm by 6 cm. A parallelogram has a base of 9 cm, a height of 6 cm and slanted sides of 8 cm. How do their areas compare?
c: The parallelogram is half as large.
items.e: Rectangle: 9 × 6 = 54 cm². Parallelogram: base × height = 9 × 6 = 54 cm². The same base and the same height give the same area. (9 × 8 = 72 uses the slanted side.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 12 × 6 = 72 m². The height is the dashed line that meets the base at a right angle. It is not the slanted 10 m side.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 7 × 4 = 28 m². The height is the dashed line that meets the base at a right angle. It is not the slanted 5 m side.

items.q: A parallelogram has an area of 96 m². Its base is 12 m. What is its height?
items.e: Area = base × height, so 12 × ? = 96. 96 ÷ 12 = 8 m. Check: 12 × 8 = 96.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 9 × 12 = 108 cm². The height is the dashed line that meets the base at a right angle. It is not the slanted 13 cm side. (Cut off the triangle at one end and slide it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 9 by 12.)

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 12 m and a height of 11 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 12 × 11 = 132 m². Do not take half: a parallelogram is a rectangle with one end cut off and moved.

items.q: This rhombus has four sides of 10 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so A = base × height = 10 × 8 = 80 cm². 10 × 10 = 100 uses a slanted side, not the height.

items.q: Cut along the dashed height and slide the triangle to the other end. What rectangle do you get?
items.e: The base stays 14 cm and the height stays 8 cm, so the rectangle is 14 cm by 8 cm. That is why the area of the parallelogram is base × height = 14 × 8 = 112 cm².

items.q: A parallelogram has an area of 63 cm². Its height is 7 cm. How long is its base?
items.e: Area = base × height, so ? × 7 = 63. 63 ÷ 7 = 9 cm. Check: 9 × 7 = 63.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 14 × 12 = 168 m². The height is the dashed line that meets the base at a right angle. It is not the slanted 15 m side.

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 24 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 24 × 6 = 144 cm². Do not take half: a parallelogram is a rectangle with one end cut off and moved.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 12 × 8 = 96 m². The height is the dashed line that meets the base at a right angle. It is not the slanted 10 m side. (Cut off the triangle at one end and slide it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 12 by 8.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 15 × 6 = 90 cm². The height is the dashed line that meets the base at a right angle. It is not the slanted 10 cm side.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 11 × 6 = 66 cm². The height is the dashed line that meets the base at a right angle. It is not the slanted 10 cm side.

items.q: Cut along the dashed height and slide the triangle to the other end. What rectangle do you get?
items.e: The base stays 9 m and the height stays 12 m, so the rectangle is 9 m by 12 m. That is why the area of the parallelogram is base × height = 9 × 12 = 108 m².

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 8 × 3 = 24 cm². The height is the dashed line that meets the base at a right angle. It is not the slanted 5 cm side. (Cut off the triangle at one end and slide it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 8 by 3.)

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 15 m and a height of 8 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 15 × 8 = 120 m². Do not take half: a parallelogram is a rectangle with one end cut off and moved.

items.q: Which number sentence gives the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × height = 15 × 12 = 180 m². 13 is the slanted side, ÷ 2 is for triangles, and 2 × (15 + 13) is the perimeter.

items.q: Which number sentence gives the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × height = 11 × 12 = 132 cm². 15 is the slanted side, ÷ 2 is for triangles, and 2 × (11 + 15) is the perimeter.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 7 × 3 = 21 cm². The height is the dashed line that meets the base at a right angle. It is not the slanted 5 cm side.

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 12 × 9 ÷ 2 = 108 ÷ 2 = 54 m². The 15 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A diagonal cuts this rectangle into two equal triangles. What is the area of the shaded triangle?
items.e: The rectangle is 14 × 5 = 70 m². The shaded triangle is half of it: 70 ÷ 2 = 35 m².

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = base × height ÷ 2 = 18 × 12 ÷ 2 = 216 ÷ 2 = 108 cm². The 15 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = base × height ÷ 2 = 6 × 4 ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm². The 5 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = base × height ÷ 2 = 11 × 12 ÷ 2 = 132 ÷ 2 = 66 m². The 20 m side is slanted, so it is not the height. Here the height falls outside the triangle and meets the grey dashed line that extends the base.

items.q: A triangle has a base of 9 cm and a height of 8 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height ÷ 2 = 9 × 8 ÷ 2 = 72 ÷ 2 = 36 cm². Do not forget to take half: a triangle is half of a rectangle or parallelogram with the same base and height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = base × height ÷ 2 = 8 × 3 ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 m². The 5 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = base × height ÷ 2 = 16 × 6 ÷ 2 = 96 ÷ 2 = 48 cm². The 10 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 12 × 5 ÷ 2 = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 m². The 13 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 3 × 4 ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm². The 5 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: Which number sentence gives the area of the triangle?
items.e: The base is 21 m and the dashed height is 12 m. A = 21 × 12 ÷ 2 = 252 ÷ 2 = 126 m². 13 m is a slanted side.

items.q: A triangle has an area of 40 m². Its height is 8 m. What is its base?
items.e: Base × height ÷ 2 = 40, so base × height = 40 × 2 = 80. Then 80 ÷ 8 = 10 m. Check: 8 × 10 ÷ 2 = 40.

items.q: A parallelogram and a triangle have the same base (10 cm) and the same height (6 cm). The area of the parallelogram is 60 cm². What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: Two copies of the triangle make a parallelogram with the same base and height. So the triangle is half: 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm². Check: 10 × 6 ÷ 2 = 30.

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 15 × 8 ÷ 2 = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 cm². The 17 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A triangle has a base of 12 m and a height of 7 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height ÷ 2 = 12 × 7 ÷ 2 = 84 ÷ 2 = 42 m². Do not forget to take half: a triangle is half of a rectangle or parallelogram with the same base and height.

items.q: A diagonal cuts this rectangle into two equal triangles. What is the area of the shaded triangle?
items.e: The rectangle is 10 × 5 = 50 m². The shaded triangle is half of it: 50 ÷ 2 = 25 m².

items.q: A triangle has a base of 16 cm and a height of 5 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height ÷ 2 = 16 × 5 ÷ 2 = 80 ÷ 2 = 40 cm². Do not forget to take half: a triangle is half of a rectangle or parallelogram with the same base and height.

items.q: A triangle has an area of 30 cm². Its base is 6 cm. What is its height?
items.e: Base × height ÷ 2 = 30, so base × height = 30 × 2 = 60. Then 60 ÷ 6 = 10 cm. Check: 6 × 10 ÷ 2 = 30.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = base × height ÷ 2 = 14 × 12 ÷ 2 = 168 ÷ 2 = 84 m². The 13 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A diagonal cuts this rectangle into two equal triangles. What is the area of the shaded triangle?
items.e: The rectangle is 10 × 7 = 70 cm². The shaded triangle is half of it: 70 ÷ 2 = 35 cm².

items.q: What is the perimeter of parallelogram B?
items.e: Add the four sides: 9 + 10 + 9 + 10 = 38 m. The dashed height is not a side. (Its area, 9 × 8 = 72 m², is the same as rectangle A.)

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 24 cm² and a length of 8 cm. What is its perimeter?
items.e: First find the width: 24 ÷ 8 = 3 cm. Then add all four sides: 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22 cm.

items.q: Each rectangle has an area of 36 m². Which one has the greatest perimeter?
items.e: The area stays 36 m², but the perimeters change: 1 × 36 → 74 m, 2 × 18 → 40 m, 4 × 9 → 26 m, 6 × 6 → 24 m. A long, thin rectangle has a large perimeter; a rectangle close to a square has a small one.

items.q: Which sentence is true?
c: Same area; B has the greater perimeter.
Same area; A has the greater perimeter.
items.e: Areas: 9 × 2 = 18 and 6 × 3 = 18, so the areas are the same. Perimeters: A: 9 + 2 + 9 + 2 = 22 cm. B: 6 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 18 cm.

items.q: Each rectangle has an area of 48 cm². Which one has the greatest perimeter?
items.e: The area stays 48 cm², but the perimeters change: 2 × 24 → 52 cm, 3 × 16 → 38 cm, 4 × 12 → 32 cm, 6 × 8 → 28 cm. A long, thin rectangle has a large perimeter; a rectangle close to a square has a small one.

items.q: Which rectangle has the same area as a 3 m by 10 m rectangle?
items.e: 3 × 10 = 30 m². 2 × 15 = 30 m² too, so the areas are equal. The other rectangles have the same perimeter (26 m) but a different area.

items.q: Which rectangle has the same area as a 4 cm by 9 cm rectangle?
items.e: 4 × 9 = 36 cm². 2 × 18 = 36 cm² too, so the areas are equal. The other rectangles have the same perimeter (26 cm) but a different area.

items.q: Each rectangle has an area of 24 cm². Which one has the least perimeter?
items.e: The area stays 24 cm², but the perimeters change: 1 × 24 → 50 cm, 2 × 12 → 28 cm, 3 × 8 → 22 cm, 4 × 6 → 20 cm. A long, thin rectangle has a large perimeter; a rectangle close to a square has a small one.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 36 cm² and a length of 12 cm. What is its perimeter?
items.e: First find the width: 36 ÷ 12 = 3 cm. Then add all four sides: 12 + 3 + 12 + 3 = 30 cm.

items.q: Rectangle A is 4 m by 6 m. Rectangle B is 3 m by 8 m. Which sentence is true?
c: Same perimeter; B has the greater area.
Same area; B has the greater perimeter.
Same area; A has the greater perimeter.
items.e: Areas: 4 × 6 = 24 m² and 3 × 8 = 24 m². Perimeters: 2 × (4 + 6) = 20 m and 2 × (3 + 8) = 22 m. Same area, different perimeters.

items.q: Which sentence is true?
c: Same area; B has the greater perimeter.
Same area; A has the greater perimeter.
items.e: Areas: 5 × 4 = 20 and 10 × 2 = 20, so the areas are the same. Perimeters: A: 5 + 4 + 5 + 4 = 18 m. B: 10 + 2 + 10 + 2 = 24 m.

items.q: A triangle has a base of 8 cm and a height of 6 cm. Which rectangle has the same area?
items.e: Triangle: 8 × 6 ÷ 2 = 24 cm². A 4 cm by 6 cm rectangle is 4 × 6 = 24 cm². (8 cm by 6 cm forgets to take half.)

items.q: Which rectangle has the same area as a 4 cm by 6 cm rectangle?
items.e: 4 × 6 = 24 cm². 3 × 8 = 24 cm² too, so the areas are equal. The other rectangles have the same perimeter (20 cm) but a different area.

items.q: Both rectangles have an area of 24 m². How much greater is the perimeter of A?
c: None. The areas are the same.

items.q: Both rectangles have an area of 24 cm². How much greater is the perimeter of A?
c: None. The areas are the same.

items.q: Rectangle A and parallelogram B have the same base and height. Which sentence is true?
c: Same area; A has the greater perimeter.
Same area; B has the greater perimeter.
items.e: Both areas are 8 × 4 = 32 cm². Perimeters: A is 2 × (8 + 4) = 24 cm and B is 2 × (8 + 5) = 26 cm. The slanted sides make B’s perimeter greater.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 45 m² and a length of 9 m. What is its perimeter?
items.e: First find the width: 45 ÷ 9 = 5 m. Then add all four sides: 9 + 5 + 9 + 5 = 28 m.

items.q: How many different rectangles with whole-number side lengths (in cm) have an area of 24 cm²? A rectangle and the same rectangle turned do not count twice.
items.e: List the pairs that multiply to 24: 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8, 4 × 6. That makes 4 rectangles.

items.q: A square has a perimeter of 24 cm. A rectangle has the same area as the square and is 9 cm long. What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Square: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 cm sides, so its area is 6 × 6 = 36 cm². Rectangle: 36 ÷ 9 = 4 cm wide. Perimeter: 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 cm. Same area, but a different perimeter.

items.q: How many different rectangles with whole-number side lengths (in cm) have an area of 18 cm²? A rectangle and the same rectangle turned do not count twice.
items.e: List the pairs that multiply to 18: 1 × 18, 2 × 9, 3 × 6. That makes 3 rectangles.

sets.title: Word problems: gardens, flags and rinks

items.q: Ethan’s family floods a backyard rink that is 12 m long and 8 m wide. What is the area of the ice?
items.e: A = length × width = 12 × 8 = 96 m². (12 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 40 m is the length of the boards around it.)

items.q: A sailboat on Lake Ontario has a sail shaped like a right triangle. The bottom edge is 3 m, the edge along the mast is 4 m and the slanted edge is 5 m. What is the area of the sail?
items.e: The bottom edge and the mast meet at a right angle, so they are the base and the height. A = 3 × 4 ÷ 2 = 6 m². The 5 m edge is slanted.

items.q: The front wall of a cottage is a rectangle 8 m wide and 3 m tall with a triangle on top that is 2 m tall. What is the area of the wall?
items.e: Rectangle: 8 × 3 = 24 m². Triangle: 8 × 2 ÷ 2 = 8 m². Total: 24 + 8 = 32 m².

items.q: Tiles shaped like parallelograms have a base of 10 cm, a height of 6 cm and slanted sides of 8 cm. What area do 30 tiles cover?
items.e: One tile: 10 × 6 = 60 cm². 30 tiles: 30 × 60 = 1800 cm². (10 × 8 uses the slanted side.)

items.q: At recess, Priya draws a parallelogram with sidewalk chalk. Its base is 60 cm, its height is 40 cm and its slanted sides are 50 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 60 × 40 = 2400 cm². The 50 cm sides are slanted, so they are not the height.

items.q: A rectangular soccer field at school has an area of 2400 m². It is 60 m long. How wide is it?
A bulletin board is 3 m long and 2 m tall. Backing paper costs $2 per square metre. How much does the paper for the board cost?
items.e: Area: 3 × 2 = 6 m². Cost: 6 × $2 = $12. ($20 comes from using the perimeter, 10 m.)

items.q: The two triangle ends of a shed roof each have a base of 4 m and a height of 3 m. What is the total area of both ends?
items.e: One end: 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 6 m². Two ends: 2 × 6 = 12 m².

items.q: Noah’s hockey team makes a triangle pennant with a base of 30 cm and a height of 50 cm. How much felt does the pennant need?
Lucas’s family plants a vegetable garden shaped like a parallelogram. Its base is 9 m and its height is 6 m. The slanted sides are 7 m long. What is the area of the garden?
items.e: A = base × height = 9 × 6 = 54 m². The 7 m sides are slanted, so they are not the height.

items.q: A Canadian flag is 180 cm long and 90 cm tall. The red band at each end is 45 cm wide and 90 cm tall. What is the area of the two red bands together?
items.e: One band: 45 × 90 = 4050 cm². Two bands: 2 × 4050 = 8100 cm².

items.q: Nathan’s class makes 10 triangle flags for a Terry Fox Run banner. Each flag has a base of 20 cm and a height of 30 cm. How much fabric do the flags use in all?
items.e: One flag: 20 × 30 ÷ 2 = 300 cm². Ten flags: 10 × 300 = 3000 cm².

items.q: A triangular flower bed has a base of 8 m and a height of 5 m. One packet of wildflower seeds covers 4 m². How many packets are needed for the whole bed?
items.e: Area: 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = 20 m². Packets: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. (Forgetting to take half gives 40 ÷ 4 = 10.)

items.q: Two classrooms both have floors of 48 m². One is 8 m by 6 m. The other is 12 m by 4 m. How much longer is the perimeter of the 12 m by 4 m room?
c: None. The areas are the same.
items.e: 8 m by 6 m: 8 + 6 + 8 + 6 = 28 m. 12 m by 4 m: 12 + 4 + 12 + 4 = 32 m. 32 − 28 = 4 m. Same area does not mean same perimeter.

items.q: Kai makes two posters with the same area, 1200 cm². One is 40 cm by 30 cm. The other is 60 cm by 20 cm. He glues ribbon around the edges. Which poster needs more ribbon, and how much more?
items.e: 40 cm by 30 cm: 40 + 30 + 40 + 30 = 140 cm. 60 cm by 20 cm: 60 + 20 + 60 + 20 = 160 cm. The 60 cm by 20 cm poster needs 160 − 140 = 20 cm more ribbon.

items.q: A park in Winnipeg is a rectangle 60 m long and 40 m wide. It has a triangular pond with a base of 20 m and a height of 10 m. The rest of the park is grass. What is the area of the grass?
A community garden shaped like a parallelogram has an area of 240 m². Its base is 20 m. What is its height?
items.e: Area = base × height, so 20 × ? = 240. 240 ÷ 20 = 12 m. (Doubling is only for triangles.)

items.q: A yield sign is a triangle. Each side is 90 cm, and its height is about 78 cm. About how much area does the sign have?
items.e: Use the 90 cm side as the base and the 78 cm height: 90 × 78 ÷ 2 = 7020 ÷ 2 = 3510 cm². 90 × 90 ÷ 2 uses a slanted side instead of the height.

items.q: A triangular sail has an area of 12 m². Its base is 4 m. How tall is the sail?
items.e: Base × height ÷ 2 = 12, so base × height = 24. Height = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 m.

items.q: Ava wants a rectangular garden with an area of 36 m² and whole-metre sides. She wants to use as little fence as possible. Which size should she choose?
items.e: All four have an area of 36 m². Perimeters: 6 by 6 → 24 m, 4 by 9 → 26 m, 3 by 12 → 30 m, 2 by 18 → 40 m. The square uses the least fence.
